Question:
The numbers from \(1\) to \(49\) are arranged in a spiral pattern on a square grid, beginning at the center. The first few numbers have been entered into the grid below. Consider the four numbers that will appear in the shaded squares, on the same diagonal as the number \(7.\) How many of these four numbers are prime?

[Figure 1](figures/2023_AMC_8_Q04_question_fig1.svg)
Solution:
Continue the spiral in the direction already shown: after \(7\), move right through \(8,9,10\), then turn upward. Each new outer layer continues around the previous one. The completed grid lets us read the shaded squares directly:

[Figure 1](figures/2023_AMC_8_Q04_official_expansion_solution_fig1.png)

The four shaded entries are \(19,23,39,47\). The number \(39=3\cdot13\) is composite. To check the other three, it is enough to test the primes \(2,3,5\): any composite number below \(49\) must have a prime factor less than \(7\). None of \(19,23,47\) is even, divisible by \(3\), or ends in \(0\) or \(5\), so all three are prime.

Thus \(\boxed{3}\) of the shaded numbers are prime, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
